findings.evidence: Both `theorem continuousOn_dslope_prod {U} (hU : Convex ℝ U) (hU_open : IsOpen U) ... : ContinuousOn ... (U ×ˢ U)` and `theorem continuousOn_dslope_prod_open {U} (hU_open : IsOpen U) ... : ContinuousOn ... (U ×ˢ U)` share the same conclusion; naming.md: hypotheses are described (via `of_`) to disambiguate the more constrained variant.
findings.fix: Rename the convex lemma to `continuousOn_dslope_prod_of_convex` and give the general open lemma the plain name `continuousOn_dslope_prod` (then `continuousOn_dslope_first_arg_open`/`deriv_dslope_bounded_on_compact_open` can drop `_open` too, since open is the default).
findings.issue: `continuousOn_dslope_prod` (requires `Convex ℝ U`) and `continuousOn_dslope_prod_open` (open `U` only) have identical conclusions; the extra convexity hypothesis is carried by the *plain* name while the more general result gets the `_open` suffix. This inverts the convention that the specialized, extra-hypothesis lemma is the one that gets the qualifier, so the plainly-named lemma silently advertises more generality than it has.

summary: Names largely describe their conclusions in standard terminology and are consistent with Mathlib's continuousOn_dslope. The one issue is that the plain name is given to the convexity-requiring lemma while its strictly more general sibling carries the _open qualifier.
